history.summary: ISKCON's Rajkot centre at Hare Krishna Land, Mota Mava, Kalawad Road (opposite Kankot Patiya), established in 2003 and inaugurated by Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi and Alfred Ford. Built under the guidance of Sri Sri Mahavishnu Goswami Maharaj, who envisioned it as a Bhakti Yoga centre. The complex includes a vegetarian restaurant, devotional shop, library, good parking, and a Gopal Goshala (cowshed); it runs kirtans, Bhagavad Gita discourses, Sunday musical aartis, Sri Prahlad Vidyalaya, Harinam Sankirtan and 'Food for Life' programs.

name: ISKCON Temple (Sri Radha Neelmadhav Dham)
town_description: Rajkot is the fourth-largest city of Gujarat and a major commercial, industrial and educational hub of the Saurashtra region. Once the capital of the princely state of Rajkot and an administrative centre of the Saurashtra region, it is also the city where Mahatma Gandhi spent his early years. The city is well connected by air (Rajkot International Airport at Hirasar), rail (Rajkot Junction) and road (NH-27).

travel.airport: Rajkot International Airport ~30 km (verify); old Civil Airport closer (verify).
travel.road: On Kalawad Road at Mota Mava; reachable by city buses, taxis and auto-rickshaws (verify distances).
